docRequirement: `agent-sdk/mcp.md:375` binds the JSON configuration surface: "For the streamable HTTP transport, use `"type": "http"` instead. In `.mcp.json` and other JSON config files, `"streamable-http"` is accepted as an alias for `"http"`. The programmatic `mcpServers` option accepts only `"http"`." So every JSON reader of an MCP server map must treat `"streamable-http"` as `"http"`, and the alias must be folded away at parse time — the programmatic/typed `mcpServers` value stays `"http"`-only, so the transport union must NOT be widened.
current: No reader in our own source knows the token. `grep -a -rn streamable` over `packages/` and `apps/` (excluding `dist/`) returns four hits, all unrelated: the MCP SDK class names `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:8, packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/proxy-tool-names.test.ts:6), `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` (packages/shared/src/mcp/pool-server.ts:31) and one prose comment (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:83). Five closed transport sets each omit the alias: (1) the `.mcp.json` reader `parseProjectMcpServer` reads `const type = raw.type` (packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:118) then branches `type === 'http' || type === 'sse'` (:119), `type === 'ws'` (:144), `type === undefined || type === 'stdio'` (:163) and `return null` (:177); its caller `parseMcpServersDocument` then emits `Ignoring ${label} server "${slug}": unsupported MCP server config` (:211) and drops the entry. (2) The Claude plugin adapter `normalizeClaudeMcpServerMap` computes `rawTransport` at packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1030-1031 and gates it at :1039-1041 on `'stdio' || 'http' || 'sse' || 'ws'`; because `??` only falls through on null/undefined, the string `'streamable-http'` blocks the `url ? 'http'` fallback, so `transport` is `undefined` and the server is rejected at :1044 with `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).` (3) The Codex adapter repeats the set minus `ws` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/codex.ts:906-908). (4) The native Nessy manifest validator rejects it with `plugin.mcp.invalid_transport` (packages/shared/src/plugins/schema.ts:610-615, inside `normalizePluginCapability`, reached from `normalizeNessyPluginManifest` at :459). (5) The inventory's `mcpTransportIdentity` accepts only `stdio|http|sse` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:452-457). MEASURED, not only read: `parseMcpServersDocument({mcpServers:{control_http:{type:'http',url:'https://example.com/mcp'},alias_streamable:{type:'streamable-http',url:'https://example.com/mcp'}}}, collect)` returns `["control_http"]` and `warnings = ["Ignoring .mcp.json server \"alias_streamable\": unsupported MCP server config"]` — the `http` entry in the same document is the positive control, so the absence is real. Nothing normalizes one layer up: the live readers hand the raw `JSON.parse` result straight in (packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:455-465, packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-contribution-detect.ts:123-129); the exported `loadProjectMcpServers` wrapper (project-config.ts:218) has no production caller — its only reference is packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/base-agent.test.ts:803. Nothing rescues it one layer down: the vendored bundles do carry the SDK's own `z.enum(["http","streamable-http"]).transform(() => "http")` under apps/electron/dist, but Pi is handed an already-parsed `Record<string, SdkMcpServerConfig>`, so the entry is gone before that schema could see it.
divergence: The transport itself is fully implemented — we speak streamable HTTP, under the name `http`, with the correct typed value in `SdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:733-735). The delta is exactly one accepted spelling at the JSON parse boundary: the documented alias `"streamable-http"` is not mapped to `"http"`. It is a key-value-name gap, not a missing capability, and the doc's third sentence means the fix must be a fold-at-parse (emit `'http'`), never a widening of the transport union. Second-order: our rejection is also quieter than a rejection should be — `parseMcpServersDocument`'s warning goes to an optional `debug` callback that defaults to a no-op (runtime-pool-servers.ts:273 `const debug = options.debug ?? (() => {})`), while the entry still appears in the capability inventory, so the user sees a listed server with no tools and no message.

change.what: ONE LINE, the whole doc-bound fix for this surface. Replace `const type = raw.type;` at :118 with `const type = raw.type === 'streamable-http' ? 'http' : raw.type;` and carry the citation in a comment (`agent-sdk/mcp.md:375` / `mcp.md:78`). The existing `http|sse` arm at :119 then runs unchanged and the object literal at :127 emits `type: 'http'`, so the value crossing into `SdkMcpServerConfig` is one the union already allows. Do not add a `'streamable-http'` member to the union.

ONE LINE. Between the `rawTransport` computation (:1030-1031) and the closed-set gate (:1039), fold the alias: `const declaredTransport = rawTransport === 'streamable-http' ? 'http' : rawTransport;` and test `declaredTransport` at :1039 instead of `rawTransport`. Needed because `??` cannot fall through a non-null string, so today a bundled `.mcp.json` with the documented spelling loses the `url ? 'http'` fallback and dies at :1044.

Positive: `{type:'streamable-http', url}` parses to `{type:'http', url}` with an empty warning list. Negative/boundary: `{type:'streamable-https'}` and `{type:'STREAMABLE-HTTP'}` are still dropped with the `unsupported MCP server config` warning (the doc names one exact literal; do not case-fold). Keep an `http` entry in the same document as the positive control, mirroring the reproduction above.

WIRE/PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY — stated explicitly because it is a risk trigger here, and because the safe design turns on it: `SdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:733) crosses into the Pi subprocess as `Record<string, SdkMcpServerConfig>` and into the persisted capability projection, and `isSdkMcpServerConfig` (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:181) recognizes only `http|sse|stdio`. Folding at parse means NO new value ever crosses that boundary, so the fix is schema-neutral; adding `'streamable-http'` to the union or to `PluginMcpDescriptor.transport` (packages/shared/src/plugins/types.ts:169) WOULD be a wire+persistence change and would also contradict the page's third sentence. Backend asymmetry to keep in mind while testing: on the Claude backend only (off by default behind `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE`), packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:305 passes `settingSources: ['user', 'project', 'local']`, so the vendored Claude Agent SDK reads project `.mcp.json` through its own loader, which does honour the alias — the same file behaves differently per backend today, and the fix removes that split.
userImpact: Concrete and silent. Many MCP servers document their own JSON as `"type": "streamable-http"`, because that is the MCP specification's name for the transport. A user who pastes that block into `.mcp.json`, `~/.nessy/mcp.json` or `.nessy-agent/mcp.json` gets a server that never connects and exposes no tools. It is not simply missing from the UI: the capability inventory keys off the server name regardless of `type` (native-sources.ts:493-503), and with `transport` unset but `url` present the panel labels it `http` via the fallback at resolver.ts:1653 — so the MCP/Sources surface lists an apparently-normal HTTP server that produces nothing. The only trace is `Ignoring .mcp.json server "<name>": unsupported MCP server config`, routed to a `debug` callback that defaults to a no-op (runtime-pool-servers.ts:273), so with no debug sink attached there is no message at all. The user's next move is to suspect their token or the server. Same for plugin install: a Claude plugin bundling a `.mcp.json` with that spelling imports with the server missing and the diagnostic `Claude MCP server requires a command (stdio) or url (http/sse/ws).`, which is misleading — the entry does have a `url`.
notes: Every cited file was read on HEAD in this session, and the `.mcp.json` behaviour was executed, not inferred: `bun run` over `parseMcpServersDocument` with an `http` positive control in the same document produced exactly the drop and the warning quoted above. The doc sentence was re-fetched with `curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp.md` and read whole at line 375 — all three sentences; the third one restricts the alias to JSON config files rather than reversing it, which is why the change list folds at parse and forbids widening the union. Two items rest on reading rather than execution: the Claude adapter rejection (claude.ts:1030-1044 — the `??` short-circuit is unambiguous, but I did not run the adapter end to end) and the assertion that no debug sink is attached on the default desktop path (I verified the default is a no-op at runtime-pool-servers.ts:273; I did not enumerate every caller that may pass one). This finding is the `agent-sdk/mcp` twin of f041 on `mcp.md:78`, which states the same rule for `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json` and `claude mcp add-json`; of those three surfaces only `.mcp.json`-shaped files exist in this fork. Fix them in one commit — the two findings share every edit.
